title: Arm A's one live deploy
lede: The Jeeves-generated QRWTY backend (baseline 33d50e9 plus Q06 ee186c1) on real Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Memorystore for Valkey and Pub/Sub in us-central1, with Auth0 as the issuer: what ran, what each probe sent and got back, and the gaps only the cloud showed. Everything here was torn down afterwards.

probes.summary: The project's one budget (USD 50 a month, alerts at 20 %, 50 % and 100 %: USD 10, 25 and 50, credits excluded, this project only) was read and reused; none was created. No qrwtya- resource and no click-events name existed. Prices were requoted from the Cloud Billing Catalog before the first apply (records/p01-inventory-before.txt, cost-quote.json).

probes.title: Push the image and pin it by digest
probes.summary: Two images were pushed to qrwtya-images: the committed baseline plus Q06 (sha256:a99d60c7…87a99, built from git archive of 1d79868) and the same app with Q13's AG-13 fix (sha256:fa158f69…fe989). Each release ran one digest in every service, the worker pool and the migration job. Cloud Run records the platform manifest the index resolves to (…e3e6d3f9ced0 and …cbcc295c049f).

probes.title: Apply network, stores, Pub/Sub, secrets and IAM
probes.summary: The saved plan's 93 resources were created in 11 min (Cloud SQL 10 min 43 s, each Memorystore instance about 5.5 min), but the apply ended in errors: CLUSTER_DISABLED Memorystore reports no discovery endpoints, so 24 IAM bindings and the outputs could not be evaluated (finding I-2). After the fixes the configuration converged: a final plan reports no changes. Cloud SQL has only a private address and requires trusted client certificates; both caches are CLUSTER_DISABLED, SERVER_AUTHENTICATION, AUTH_DISABLED; the analytics subscription reads back ack 60 s, retry 1–10 s, dead letter after 100, retention 31 days, no expiry.

probes.title: Bootstrap credentials without printing them
probes.summary: 15 credentials (14 database credentials and the link-replay-keys ring) were generated locally and piped to Secret Manager; the postgres admin's password was set through the SQL Admin API from the same value. No value is in the plan, the state, a log or this record. The two Memorystore CA versions are public certificates in state.

probes.title: Migrations as a release job with a non-superuser admin
probes.summary: The first two executions timed out connecting (the job had no VPC egress to the private-IP instance: finding I-4). After the fix, two executions started together: one applied every template migration, the other waited on the advisory lock and applied only the module SQL; a third applied no template migration. All exit 0. The admin (postgres) is CREATEDB CREATEROLE, not superuser, and has no CONNECT on the four application databases; PUBLIC has none; Link API's login can CREATE in no schema; the never-delete trigger refuses a DELETE (QRW10).

probes.title: Auth0 issuer and A's audience on the generated guard
probes.summary: From the VPC (the probe job on Session API's subnet and NAT), the tenant's discovery document names exactly OIDC_ISSUER, with its trailing slash, and its key set URL. A client-credentials token for https://api.qrwtya.qrwty.io was accepted by Link API's guard (signedIn true); the same token with its audience changed, a foreign issuer's self-signed token, A's issuer signed by a key outside the key set, a malformed bearer and A's token after its 60 s lifetime were each refused 401. probes.title: Providers from Cloud Run: Web Risk and Stripe

gaps.where: module-clients.ts.template (externalTarget: 'the client reads no credential'); jeeves-generator README
gaps.gap: An External API client has no workload-identity credential. A stub that calls a Google API (Web Risk) can only add a header itself; the documented way is a credential from a SECRET_DIR file, i.e. a long-lived API key. On Cloud Run, Link API's Q06 code got 403 from Web Risk and every guest create failed closed (503).
gaps.workaround: Application files: link-operations/google-credentials.ts fetches Link API's service-account token from the metadata server (cached, monotonic, one deadline with the lookup) when QRWTY_REPUTATION_CREDENTIALS=metadata; the production profile requires that value. 9 unit tests.

gaps.gap: Tile-to-tile calls carry no ID token, so Cloud Run's invoker IAM can't protect a service another tile calls: such a service must be internal-only with IAM off, and any VPC caller can reach it. A public origin can be IAM-protected only if no tile calls it (Billing API had to become internal; Stripe webhooks would need it public).
gaps.workaround: IaC: internal ingress with IAM off for Link, Account and Billing API; IAM required for the public Redirect and Session origins (no allUsers).

gaps.gap: The generated health route /healthz is a path Cloud Run's front end reserves: <service>.run.app/healthz answers Google's 404 page before the container. Only Cloud Run's own startup and liveness probes reach it, so no edge, uptime check or tile can read a process's health over HTTP.
gaps.workaround: None needed for this deploy (Cloud Run's probes work); P09 used the sign-in me routes to show reachability.

gaps.where: module-clients.ts.template (pubsubPublisher, pubsubLoop: new PubSub without apiEndpoint)
gaps.gap: The Pub/Sub clients always use the global endpoint and have no regional-endpoint binding. The durable-clicks contract pins storage to us-central1 with in-transit enforcement; Pub/Sub then refuses any request the global endpoint routes to another region (FAILED_PRECONDITION, seen from outside the region). The generated publisher and worker work only because Google routes them to us-central1.
gaps.workaround: None in the app; operators pull dead letters through https://us-central1-pubsub.googleapis.com/. Remedy: JEEVES_PUBSUB_ENDPOINT, required when the topic enforces in transit.

gaps.gap: A process logs 'Application ready' but nothing when SIGTERM arrives, when its drain starts or ends, or with what code it exits; Cloud Run logs no exit for a service instance either. A rollout's drain can't be shown from logs (P10).
gaps.workaround: P10 shows the drain by traffic instead: 1,501 requests during the rollout, none failed.

findings.finding: Q04b: tofu validate passed at once; only tofu fmt failed (locals.tf alignment).
findings.fix: tofu fmt; validate.sh exits 0 (fmt 0, init 0, validate 0); lint self-test 8/8.

findings.finding: A CLUSTER_DISABLED Memorystore instance reports no discovery_endpoints (deprecated, empty). The first apply created all 93 resources' worth of stores but failed evaluating the cache variables, so 24 secret IAM bindings and the outputs were never applied.
findings.fix: locals.cache_primary: the PSC auto connection of type CONNECTION_TYPE_PRIMARY (address and port); outputs use it.

findings.finding: Each Memorystore instance has its own managed CA (GOOGLE_MANAGED_PER_INSTANCE_CA); the IaC had one CA secret from hot-routes, which Link API's admission-cache would have refused.
findings.fix: One public CA secret per cache (qrwtya-memorystore-ca-<cache>), mounted for the one process that uses it; the probe shows the other instance's CA is refused.

findings.finding: The migration job had no VPC egress: the Cloud SQL connector couldn't reach the private-only instance and both first executions timed out (pg 'timeout expired' after 5 s, uncaught).
findings.fix: vpc_access (Direct VPC egress, ALL_TRAFFIC) on the job, as on the services.

findings.finding: Cloud Run's Direct VPC egress with ALL_TRAFFIC leaves no Internet route: Auth0's key set, the tenant origin and Stripe need a NAT. Added before the first apply. Measured: a fresh task's first connection through the NAT failed for 12 s and 48 s in two runs, a second destination for about 4 s; Google APIs over Private Google Access worked at once.
findings.fix: qrwtya-router and qrwtya-nat (AUTO_ONLY, the run subnet only).

findings.finding: Pub/Sub reads the archive (Cloud Storage) subscription's ack deadline back as 300 s; the IaC said 60, a perpetual diff.
Cloud Run returns secret volumes before the Cloud SQL volume; the IaC's order made every plan show a reorder of all six resources.
findings.fix: Secret volumes and mounts first; the final plan reports no changes.

findings.finding: The services declared no traffic block, so P11's manual pin (gcloud --no-traffic) survived the image-2 apply: Session API kept serving image 1 with a dangling tag.
findings.fix: traffic { LATEST 100 } on every service; the next apply moved Session API to its latest revision and dropped the tag.

findings.finding: Billing API was public (for Stripe webhooks through the edge), but tile clients can't authenticate to an IAM-protected origin (AG-14) and no edge exists in this release.
findings.fix: Billing API internal; public origins (Redirect, Session) require Cloud Run IAM. The qrwty.io Worker route was not added: it would need proxy code, not only a route, and an edge credential the origin can verify.

findings.finding: Additions the Q06 handoff asked for and the cloud needs.
findings.fix: Secret link-replay-keys (mounted for Link API), QRWTY_PUBLIC_ORIGIN_URL = https://qrwty.io, webrisk.googleapis.com in the API list, QRWTY_REPUTATION_CREDENTIALS = metadata with image 2.
